analysis.title: China tech is crashing but the real problem is much bigger
key_insights: ChiNext closed at its lowest level since August 2025. It is far below its 200-day moving average, and the 100-day average has crossed below the 200-day, a rare technical signal of a deteriorating trend.
US tech has been riding the AI boom while Chinese tech has fallen sharply. The report says winning the technology race and making money for shareholders are not the same thing.
ChiNext weekly RSI is approaching extremely oversold territory, but earlier washouts saw more extreme readings. Oversold can persist and RSI alone is not a buy signal.
BofA reports $17bn of inflows into Chinese equity funds in the week ended October 21, the largest since July. The CSI 300 is down 20% since June and its technology sector is down 41%.
China equity funds have had roughly $177bn of net outflows year-to-date. Dip buying has returned but there is little evidence of a sustained reversal in investor appetite.

Goldman: high-tech sectors are 38% of industrial production and 18% of investment but only 11% of employment. Each RMB1mn of final spending supports about three jobs in high-tech versus 4.6 in property.

Goldman estimates most major housing activity indicators are down 60-90% from their 2020-21 peaks. Property is expected to subtract 1.8 percentage points from GDP growth this year, and it is more than half of household assets.

China shows a deflationary combination: falling equities, government bond yields at record lows around 1.6%, and the renminbi at a four-year high against the dollar. Property investment is still contracting about 20% y/y despite lower borrowing costs. Hartnett describes a consumer and investor buyer strike.

BofA's Hartnett cites Chinese exports up 36% y/y, with high-tech exports up 63%. Export strength is disconnected from domestic demand, raising the risk of exporting deflation and squeezing corporate earnings globally.

Credit Agricole says broad fiscal spending remained in contraction and the deficit has undershot the budget. October new home and auto sales both fell more than 20% y/y. The bank expects a Q4 fiscal acceleration, with government bond issuance potentially reaching RMB4tn versus RMB2.3tn a year ago.

sector_views.rationale: The sector is in a technical downtrend. CSI 300 technology is down 41% since June and ChiNext is at its lowest since August 2025. The report says oversold is not a reversal signal.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Lower yields are not reviving property or demand, which is consistent with a deflation trap.
Exports are strong while domestic demand is weak, so China may be exporting deflation to other economies.
Easier financing costs have not stopped the property decline.

macro_indicators.indicator: China new home and auto sales
macro_indicators.interpretation: October high-frequency data show weak domestic demand.

macro_indicators.reading: -1.8 percentage points from GDP growth this year
macro_indicators.interpretation: Goldman expects the drag to fade only gradually.

macro_indicators.reading: RMB4tn potential in Q4 versus RMB2.3tn a year ago
macro_indicators.interpretation: Credit Agricole expects a Q4 fiscal acceleration that could support domestic demand.

macro_indicators.reading: renminbi at a four-year high against the dollar
macro_indicators.interpretation: A stronger renminbi alongside falling equities and yields fits the report's deflationary pattern.

risk_factors: Further downside in Chinese equities, since oversold conditions can persist.
Continued property decline, with household wealth and consumption effects.
Chinese deflation exported through high-tech exports, squeezing corporate earnings globally.
Fiscal stimulus may fail to lift domestic demand, or deliver only a temporary bounce.
Consumer and investor buyer strike that lower yields do not break.

tension_points.bear_case: Funds have had about $177bn of outflows year-to-date. ChiNext is in a technical downtrend, property is a major drag, and domestic demand is weak despite record low yields.
